snapshot.name: Polycab India Ltd
snapshot.about: Polycab is India’s leading manufacturers of cables and wires and allied products such as uPVC conduits and lugs and glands. We have a range of cables and wires for practically every application. More recently Polycab has also launched a wide range of consumer electrical products like Fans, Switches, Switchgear, LED lights and Luminaries, Solar Inverters, and Pumps.

latest_quarter.source: screener quarterly table (standardised from exchange filing)
latest_quarter.headline: Revenue +53% YoY, EBITDA +39%, PAT +43%, margin 14.4% (-1.4pp YoY)

notes.text: Capex in progress: CWIP is 35% of fixed assets — growth capacity not yet earning
Working capital tightening: cash conversion cycle 65 → 39 days
5-yr cumulative CFO is 1.01× PAT (₹8,856 Cr vs ₹8,756 Cr)
5-yr free cash flow ₹4,592 Cr; negative in 1 of 5 years

business_mix.what_it_does: Polycab India Limited manufactures and sells wires, cables, fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG), and undertakes EPC projects.

segments.name: Wires and Cables
segments.note: Includes domestic wires, cables, and exports

segments.name: FMEG
segments.note: Includes solar products, fans, lighting, switches, switchgear, conduits, pipes, and fittings

narrative_vs_numbers.management_says: Long-term EBITDA margins are expected to be around 11% to 13%.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers_say: Reported OPM % has consistently hovered around 11% to 16% over the reported quarters.

promises.credibility: Management guidance is largely focused on long-term horizons through FY30, making most targets pending verification against final delivery.

bull: Revenue grew 53 percent year-over-year in Sep 2026 with EBITDA up 39 percent and PAT up 43 percent.
Strong returns with ROCE at 33.2 percent and ROE at 23.6 percent, alongside a steady 3-year revenue CAGR of 27 percent.
Exceptional financial health shown by investments of 4,032 crore exceeding borrowings of 272 crore with a Debt-to-Equity of 0.02.
bear: EBITDA margin dropped 1.4 percentage points year-over-year to 14.4 percent in the latest quarter Sep 2026.
Capex in progress with CWIP at 35 percent of fixed assets represents growth capacity that is not yet earning.
Free cash flow was negative in 1 out of the past 5 years despite a 5-year cumulative FCF of 4,592 crore.
